title: Average cost bounded by worst-case cost
statement: Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $\\Omega$ be a finite nonempty input alphabet, let $\\alpha$ be an output set, and let $f:\\Omega^n\\to\\alpha$. For any randomized decision tree $T$ computing $f$ and any probability distribution $\\mu$ on the input space, the average query cost of $T$ under $\\mu$ is at most its worst-case query cost over all inputs.
hypotheses_covered: $T$ is a randomized decision tree computing $f$
$\\mu$ is a probability mass function on the input space
